THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU): (a) There is only one National Sports University (NSU) in the
country which is being set up in Manipur (Imphal).
(b) The stage of requirement of coaches in NSU has not yet come. NSU is presently
running two Under Graduate and one Post Graduate degree programmes which do not
require coaches.
(c) Central Government does not appoint coaches for States. The list of foreign
coaches appointed on contract by Sports Authority of India (SAI) for National Sports
Federations (NSFs) is in the Statement (See below).
(d) The Central Government does not appoint coaches for States. SAI has 882
regular and 16 contract coaches presently working for training facilities.
(e) Development of coaches and improving their competency is an ongoing
process. Central Government is supporting NSFs under Human Resource Development
Scheme (HRDS) for aproving competency of Indian coaches. In the Annual Calendar for
Training and Competitions (ACTC) meetings with various NSFs it has been impressed
upon them to work ouappropriate training competency and upgradation programmes of
Indian coaches. National Institute of Sports, Patiala and National Sports University, Manipur
are running academic Programmes for developing coaches. The Government has taken a
decision to set up National Centre for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR).

SHRI D. RAJA (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I move:
“That this House disapproves the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation (Amendment)
Ordinance, 2019 (No.8 of 2019) promulgated by the President of India on 1st March,
2019.”
MR. CHAIRMAN: Do you want to say something?
SHRI D. RAJA: Sir, in fact, you have given me this opportunity. We are a Parliament
which is very vibrant that way. Then, why does the Government resort to ordinance route
when there is no urgency? In fact, on the eve of elections, more than ten ordinances were
issued by the Government. Why should we resort to ordinances when the Parliament is

going to meet? When the Parliament is meeting, everything can be discussed, debated in
it? If there is any urgency, even the Opposition agrees with the Government, and we also
ask the Government to issue an ordinance if the issue is such and it affects the whole
country and all sections of the people. But, here, these are very sensitive issues, very
important issues which need thorough discussion and deliberation by the Parliament.
That is why, we think this ordinance route should be given up by the Government and the
Bills will have to be referred to the Department-Related Standing Committees. The Indian
Parliament has mechanism of Standing Committees which is hailed by several other
countries. People come from different countries to study as to how the Committee System
works in Indian Parliament. Even the former President and former Vice-President, Shri K.R.
Narayanan hailed the committe System of Indian Parliament. When such a thing is available,
why should the Government not refer the Bills to the Standing Committees? And, in Rajya
Sabha, why cannot the Government agree to send certain Bills to the Select Committees?
These are certain general observations, and I wish the Government give due consideration
to what we say. We are speaking all these things in the interest of our democracy; our
parliamentary democracy; the sovereignty of our parliamentary democracy. This is what I
am pleading with the Government. Sir, I move the Statutory Resolution.

SHRI S. R. BALASUBRAMONIY AN (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, Jammu
and Kashmir is under the President’s Rule. When a State goes under the President’s Rule,
it is imposed under Article 356 of the Constitution. It is incapable of having an elected
Government right now. That is why, it has gone under the President’s Rule. The President
dissolved the Assembly and ordered the Centrally-appointed Governor to execute the
operations of the State. Every proclamation under Article 356 must be laid before both the
Houses of Parliament. It has already been laid before the Lok Sabha. Now, it is under the
consideration of the Rajya Sabha. Both the Houses should agree to this Proclamation.
The State itself came into India under the peculiar circumstances. When India got the
Independence, Pakistan was also given Independence. We wanted one India, but, they

made it two, one is Pakistan-dominion and the other is Indian-dominion. The Britishers
gave option to the States, that they could join any dominion they wanted or they could
function independently; they should choose their position themselves. That was the
position. Most of the States came under India in this region. But, two States, one was the
Hindu-majority State where a Muslim was the ruler and the other was a Muslim-majority
State, where a Hindu was the ruler. Jammu and Kashmir was under Maharaja Hari Singh.
He refused to join Indian dominion and he said, they would function separately. In the
same way, Hyderabad was also under the Nizam. They said that they would not join India.
So, after sometime, the State of Kashmir was raided by tribals backed Pakistani Army. The
State of Kashmir was not prepared to face them. So, Maharaja Hari Singh appealed to Pt.
Jawahar Lal Nehru to intervene immediately. Jawahar Lal Nehru laid two conditions. Number
one, Maharaja Hari Singh should abdicate step down immediately, and number two, Kashmir
should merge with India, that is, accession to India. Maharaja Hari Singh agreed for both.
That is how Kashmir came to India. After that, several developments happened there and
several things have happened so far. So, now under peculiar circumstances, the State is
under the President’s Rule. I have not forgotten that. Nobody can forget it also. Under
Article 356 of the Constitution, in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a State, the
Central Government appoints the Governor to execute everything on behalf of the Centre.
That is the position. Now, we are considering this Proclamation. We are not against the
Proclamation because there is no Government in place and there cannot be a Government
within a few days. Now, unless these two Houses approve, it is not possible to have
President’s Rule there at all. So, till the elections are held, there must be a Central rule only.
The only thing which I am not able to understand is, elections were held for Lok Sabha
recently, the election to the State Assembly also could have been held along with it. But,
I donot understand as to why they did not conduct the State elections also simultaneously.
Anyway, since it is not possible to carry out the governance in the State without the
President’s Rule till the elections are held, we are not against this Proclamation now. But,
our request is that the Home Ministry must make efforts to conduct elections as early as
possible. At present, Amarnath Yatra is going on. I hope, after the Amarnath Yatra, at least,
there will be elections for the State Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir, and there will be a
duly elected Government in place there. Thank you, Sir.

ratified by the new Jammu and Kashmir Assembly? That is my apprehension. Suppose a

otherwise, then what will happen? That is my apprehension. I would request the hon.
Home Minister to clarify this.

of many changes in law and many observations in the orders of the hon. Supreme Court.

administration. As Mr. Derek was very rightly pointing out and other Members have also

SHRI K.K. RAGESH (Kerala): Sir, I stand to oppose the Resolution moved here to
extend the President’s Rule for another six months’ period. Sir, it is going to be a provocative
action and it is going to be a resultant in the further alienation of the people of Kashmir. Sir,
alienation will not stop terrorism. It is going to result in the growth of terrorism. The hon.
Home Minister must take note of that. Sir, as many other hon. Members have already
explained here, if Parliament election was possible to be conducted, why cannot you
conduct the Assembly elections immediately? How can you justify that? Sir, as majority of
the political parties in the State of Jammu and Kashmir are demanding immediate election,
let us go for an immediate election so that the people of Kashmir can be involved in the
democratic process. Sir, it is very clear that the present Government’s Kashmir plot has
proved to be a failure. It has proved to be a debacle. What is your Kashmir policy and what
is the outcome of that policy? Please let me know whether the terror attacks have been
reduced. Sir, please let me know whether the ceasefire violations have been reduced. Sir,
please let me know whether the killing of civilians has been reduced. Sir, please let me
know whether the killing of our security personnel has been reduced. No, Sir. Then how
can you claim that your Kashmir Policy is a success? Sir, it is an utter debacle. Sir, from
2009-2014, a total of 109 terror attacks took place and during your period, it has increased
to 626. Sir, prior to your period, 139 security personnel were killed and during your period,
it has increased to 210. Sir, prior to your period, 12 civilians were killed and during your
period, it has increased to more than 300. So far as ceasefire violations are concerned, prior
to your period it was 563, and now, they have been alarmingly increased to 5,595. What
more to say that your Kashmir plot has turned to be a debacle. If you look at the alienation
that is being taking place in the State of Jammu and Kashmir, numerous local youths are
joining terror outfits and the number is alarmingly increasing. Sir, from 2009 to 2014, -- and
I am talking on the basis of the data of the Government itself --16 youths had joined terror
outfits. Now, it has increased to 191. Why? It is because of the alienation that is happening
there and it is due to the policy that you are implementing there. You are trying to build an
empire on the dead bodies of your own people. You are trying to divide the people on
communal lines. Sir, all the parties are united in fighting against terror. All political parties,
cutting across political lines, are opposed to terror. But, you are trying to manipulate it as

On 10th July, 1950, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah wrote to Nehruji, “I can willingly go
down and sacrifice myself for you. I have several times stated that we acceded to India
because we saw there were two bright stars of hope and aspiration; one, ‘you’, that is,
Nehruji and the other is Gandhi.” Sir, let us not forget history. ...(Interruptions)...
ÁÖß ˆ¯ÖÃÖ³ÖÖ¯Ö×ŸÖ: ¬Ö®μÖ¾ÖÖ¤ü… ´ÖÖ®Ö®ÖßμÖ Ã¾Ö¯Ö®Ö ¤üÖÃÖÝÖã¯ŸÖÖ •Öß, You have four minutes, please.
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS
(SHRI V. MURALEEDHARAN): Sir, in case he wants more time, we can extend it to him.
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: I have no objection because you have to manage the
time.
SHRI SW APAN DASGUPTA (Nominated): Sir, in the eleventh century, an Arab
traveller called All Barooni came to this country. One of the observations All Barooni made
was that the Hindus have no sense of history. I think, after listening to this debate, we
have rather an excessive sense of history because it seems history is only guiding whatever
the discussions here are. Sir, it is not merely history; it is also a question of emotion. Why,
for example, should I, a person who was born in what Lok Sabha terms is called the Kolkata
South Constituency, be concerned about what is happening in Jammu and Kashmir? Sir,
the reason for it is very simple. Sir, in 1952, we elected a Member of Parliament from Kolkata
South. His concern obviously was Bengal and he gave his life in Srinagar. His name was
Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee who some people consider a very controversial figure. I
consider him a very heroic figure and I am very glad my friend, Shri Prasanna Acharya
referred to the contribution of Shri Biju Patnaik in 1948 when the case of Kashmir was
being so hotly debated and fought over. Sir, we can go on and on about where someone
did right and where someone did wrong. But at today’s point, I think it is very important to
know that after 70 years where is the broad consensus that has taken us and I think there
is a broad consensus which has emerged. The first is that democracy in Jammu and
Kashmir is not negotiable. Whatever may have been the case from 1952-57, the aberration
of 1987 will never be repeated and I think that is the national consensus. So, democracy,
Number one, is the net national game. The second important thing which has happened is
that the idea that we must look at Jammu and Kashmir only through the prism of Kashmir
Valley has disappeared. But we must look at Jammu and Kashmir as one entity which
Government Bill

380 [RAJYA SABHA]
includes Ladakh, which includes Jammu. Sir, some people would say, ‘Oh, this is actually
communalising the whole thing.’ But, Sir, if hypothetically speaking, the population of
Jammu, for example, was to exceed that of the rest, would we say that their representation
should be curbed, that the constituencies should be made in such a way that they will not
have the equal, rightful share? That, Sir, cannot be. We cannot have it both ways and
therefore, it is very important, Sir, that we accept the logic of the reservation policy, that
people in Jammu have been deprived for so long. For whatever reasons, I am not even
going into the historical reasons, and there are good historical reasons to explain. They
have to be accommodated and made equal citizens of India. That wasn't the case and I
think, that is another net national game. The third net national game, Sir, is that for the first
time, maybe not for the first time, but certainly in a more concerted way we are once again
talking about the large numbers of people who are made refugees in their own country
through a very unfortunate process of what might loosely be called ethnic cleansing. We
haven't been able to do justice to all the people who left Kashmir, but at least we are no
longer taking the fig leaf by saying, ‘Oh, they left voluntarily. They were driven out by the
Governor.’ All these are spurious excuses. Today, the rehabilitation of those people form
a very important part of the national consensus with all sides of the House agreeing and
finally, Sir, on this question of terrorism, there is, despite everything, a national consensus
and the national consensus which manifested itself at various times. There might be big
differences over tactics etc., but there has to be zero tolerance and I think, this whole
spurious question of we must go into the roots of terrorism; we must go into their alienation
aspect; we must look at that, we must look at the psycho profile of people. We have to get
over that. Today, there is a national determination also expressed in the course of the
elections that this cannot go on. And, I think, people who say otherwise risk swimming
against the national tide; they risk actually going against the very sentiments of the
people. Whether there is terrorism in Kupwara or there is terrorism in Mumbai, we are
against all of it. And, I think, this spurious psycho explanation has to go once and for all.
I hope the hon. Home Minister is listening that there is today a complete determination, a
complete backing of your policy to resolutely fight terrorism. Sir, this is not an international
issue. I think, sometimes we make a mistake of talking about Kashmir as if it is a great
international issue. It is something deeply-felt domestic issue that affects people right
from Kargil down to Kerala. It is also not a question of only three constituencies in the
whole of India. What happens in Kashmir affects us deeply. And, therefore, it is very good
that a passionate debate of this nature is actually being held. And, I think, that national
consensus that we have managed to actually forge, and it is important to bring out the
strengths, will guide us in future. Thank you very much, Sir.
[Shri Swapan Das Gupta]

SHRIMA TI VIJILA SATHYANANTH (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, the Union
Cabinet has approved the extension of President’s Rule in Jammu and Kashmir for a
further period of six months with effect from July 3rd, 2019 under Article 356 (4) of the
Constitution of India.
This is likely to be the last extension of the Centre’s rule in the State as the Election
Commission has issued a statement recently stating that elections in Jammu and Kashmir
would be announced after the annual Amarnath Yatra which is beginning on July Ist. The
present term of President’s Rule is expiring on July 2 and the Governor has recommended
that the President’s Rule may be extended for a further period of six months. The President’s
role during the imposition will be based on a report prepared by the affected S tate’s
Governor. The President will only exercise those powers that are approved by both the
Houses of Parliament. Imposition of President’s Rule is nothing new to India. It has
happened many times. Indian States have faced the President’s Rule for a total number of
124 times in the past.
Government Bill

394 [RAJYA SABHA]
In response to a question, the Ministry of Home Affairs has mentioned that President’s
Rule has been imposed for a maximum number of times in the State of Uttar Pradesh, it
happened ten times, and, In the State of Punjab, it was imposed there for more than 3,000
days.
Sir, the BJP and the PDP were two different ideologies where one believed in strict
action against the terror forces, that is, the BJP , and, the other defended the stonepelters
and let the terrorists walk free.
As far as imposition of Governor Rule is concerned, it is merely the Governor’ s
control over the State. There is no political drama in this. Hence, the Central Government
would effectively work in the State and the Army will get the freedom to carry on the
operations to drag out the terror forces from Kashmir. So, the Governor’s rule will bring
with itself the pressure of re-elections from the various Opposition parties. The Governor’s
rule is necessary after all the mess experienced in Jammu and Kashmir in the recent times.
So, it is needed and I support it.
The debate continues over unfettering the State and granting them some sort of
autonomy. Autonomy is desired not only by the Valley; Jammu and Ladakh are seeking
regional autonomy within the same narrow confines. But with the Sunni-dominated V alley
holding the entire State to ransom, it stands to reason that other divisions also require to
be unshackled. What constitutes this so-called autonomy within the purview of the Indian
Constitution as well as Article 370 giving special status to the State enshrined in the same
Constitution? Indian Prime Ministers have spoken of an architecture within the confines
of the same Constitution.
It is a seventy year old issue. Former Prime Minister, Shri P.V . Narasimha Rao, said in
the Parliament, “So far as granting autonomy to the State of Jammu and Kashmir is
concerned, only sky is the limit. In this context, the Constitution of our country has a lot
of room and short of Azadi, we are ready to give anything.” Now, our Prime Minister,
Shri Narendra Modi says that he is willing to architect a permanent solution within the
boundaries of the Constitution because it is a humanitarian issue also.
There have been all-Party delegations from 2010 onwards, and, now recently also,
there was an all-Party delegation which visited the Valley. There was another opinion
shared by the Chairman of the All Jammu and Kashmir Awami Action Committee stating
that “it is not merely political dispute. India should look at it as humanitarian issue.
Sentiments in the V alley are for freedom and India ought to respect that. Sitting in Kashmir,
[Shrimati Vijila Sathyananth]
Government Bill

395[1 July, 2019]
we come to the conclusion that the people of India are so ill-informed about Kashmir.
Kashmir is an internationally accepted dispute. It is time to call a spade a spade.” This was
one sort of thing.
The Instrument of Accession, executed in October 1947, under which Maharaja Hari
Singh handed over the State to India, had three specific clauses. One of the salient features
of the Delhi Agreement of July 1952 was to abolish the hereditary Dogra dynasty. There
are so many clauses. There is no difference of opinion with respect to the accession of
State with India on two main issues, i.e., the Instrument of Accession and the Delhi
Agreement. The rest of the powers, including residual sovereignty, are vested with the
State under Article 370. All the Princely States were authorized to frame their own
Constitution in their respective Constituent Assemblies. At that time, only four States - -
Saurashtra, Travancore and Cochin, Mysore and J&K - - chose this option and set up
their own Constituent Assemblies. Three of these States did not frame their Constitution,
and only J&K formed its own Constituent Assembly and framed its Constitution, which
exists to this day.
Our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has two-pronged approach which may well
work. These are: mainstreaming the separatists, and empowering a newly-elected
Government to open a dialogue with the people and the hardliners. Now we are on the
right path. The “permanent solution” that our Prime Minister wants to do would materialize
under the theory of elasticity, expanding the scope and size of autonomy. And I am sure
that our Prime Minister would bring a meaningful break from the past and lead the way to
find a transformative solution. Thank you, Sir.

400 [RAJYA SABHA]
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (DR. SATYANARAYAN JATIY A): Shri T.K.S. Elangovan.
You have only four minutes at your disposal.
SHRI T.K.S. ELANGOV AN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I would take lesser than that. There are
only two issues. One is the extension of President’s Rule in the State. The other is the
replacement of an Ordinance by way of an Amendment Bill. I want to talk about this
Ordinance route. During the interregnum between the last Session and this Session, this
Government had passed ten Ordinances. Why? It is because they do not want to have
faith in the Parliament. They want to do certain things somehow as ‘vote-catcher’, which
would help them in garnering votes. These are all very simple things. Giving reservation to
the Kashmiris, increasing the reservation percentage is a welcome measure. We are in
support of that but the Government did not take this House into confidence for that and
they have brought an Ordinance. There were almost ten Ordinances. Never in the history
of India during the last seventy years that during the interregnum between two Sessions,
so many Ordinances were passed. This is the first time, it has happened. It shows that the
Government wants to take advantage of the Ordinance route for their electoral gains
beyond which I do not want to say anything.
Secondly, the Government have accepted that they could not conduct one nation,
one election. They have extended the President’s Rule in Kashmir. Just two months back,
elections to Parliament were held. They could not hold even one State election together
with the Parliament election. That shows that they could not fulfill their promise or they
could not go past what they have been talking about. Sir, nothing has happened in Kashmir.
In fact, the Government was dissolved. The President’s Rule was imposed only because
of failure of a fax machine. We know that. The Governor could not get the fax letter from the
person who wanted to become Chief Minister, so the President’s Rule was announced.
These are all flimsy things. The Governor should have waited and called the leaders and
asked whether they could form the Government. That is how the Governor should act.
Whereas the Governor in Kashmir did not follow the procedure simply stating that I have
not received the letter from the person, so, I am dissolving the Assembly and recommending
President’s Rule. But you could not conduct election simultaneously with the Parliament
elections and you talk of one nation, one election theory.
Sir, usage of Article 356 is restricted by the Judgment of S.R. Bommai’s case but this
Government has another way to circumvent that Judgment. I do not know what the necessity
for extending the President’s Rule in the State for a further period of six months is. The
Government has not explained that. What is the necessity? Why should not there be a
State Government? Why do you want to rule that State from here? Why should Delhi have
to rule Kashmir? Why not elections? Why not the people of Kashmir select their
Government?

So, this shows that the Government has no faith in democracy. This Government has
no faith in constituting a Government in the State to rule them. I oppose this extension of
President’s Rule. Of course, I welcome the reservation. But, I am against the ordinance
route. Anyhow, that is a welcome measure. That will do good to the people of Kashmir.
But, extension of President’s Rule is against democracy, against all natural laws. With
these words, I conclude. Thank you.

on the increase. Sir, in 2019 only, figures say that 162 people were killed in Kashmir valley.

called ‘Bunch of Thoughts’ in which hon. Golwalkarji has stated that in an Indian State,
Indian people who are in minority, if they want to live in this country as citizens, they
should be paying allegiance to nation’s religion, nation’s culture and nation’s language.

ideal and concept which talk about country’s religion, country’s culture, country’s language.

civilization. ...(Time-bell)... That is to be taken in mind.

point.

SHRI V . VIJAY ASAI REDDY (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Chairman. Sir, the
Statutory Resolution that has been moved by the hon. Home Minister has to be supported
and the YSR Congress Party is extending the support for five reasons. Sir, I am very
simple; I am not getting into the past. On five counts, it has to be supported. Firstly, as our
opposition colleagues have pointed out, there is no conducive atmosphere and violence
is unabated. As such, the atmosphere is not conducive to hold elections. Therefore, the
President’s Rule has to be extended. Secondly, the Assembly has been dissolved. It is not
in suspended animation. Therefore, there is no way that two or more political parties can
come together and form the Government at this point of time. Thirdly, Sir, some of the hon.
Members have pointed out if Parliamentary elections can be held, why Assembly elections
can’t. Our contention is that parliamentary elections can never be compared with that of
the Assembly elections because in Assembly elections the issues are localised. Fourthly,
if this Statutory Resolution is not accepted and passed by this august House, there could
be a constitutional crisis. Therefore, it has to be extended. Finally, Sir, in the interest of the
national security, it has to be extended. Therefore, we extend the support.
*Not Recorded.
Government Bill

413[1 July, 2019]
Coming to the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation (Amendment) Bill, it is definite that
we extend our support to the Reservation Bill also. Sir, those who reside in border areas,
whether it is an actual Line of Control or international border, there is always tension. So,
people who live in border areas live with tension. Any time anything may happen. Their
lives are in danger... there could be attacks from Pakistani side or the other side of the
border. Therefore, they are always in tension. Cross-border tension causes economic
hardship. Many times the military ask the local residents to vacate their areas which
adversely affects the education and other facilities of the people residing there. And,
because they are evacuated very often and they are very much disturbed, their interest is
to be protected either by giving them financial aid or providing the reservation. Sir, there
has to be a level-playing field. When level-playing field is to be created, obviously, either
financial help or reservations or both should be provided to those persons who are residing
around the international border, and as the Bill specifies, it is 10 kilometres from the
international border. Sir, as we are extending the area, the number of aspirants covered
under the reservation will go up, and the jobs will remain the same, I request the hon.
Home Minister to increase the number of jobs so that the opportunities will not come
down for the persons who are residing around the international border. About the policy
formation, Sir, the Government may frame the policies but they are to be implemented.
There is a need to ensure that the policies are implemented. The State has got hilly region
and rugged terrain with extreme temperatures, more in winter months. Some of the areas in
the State also face the connectivity issues. So, all these issues are to be addressed. Sir,
there is only one final point. The policies are framed by the Government, policies are to be
implemented by the Government, and for persons who do not get the benefit and who are
aggrieved by the fact that they are not getting the benefit, there has to be an authority, be
it a regulatory authority or any authority which can be approached by the persons who
are aggrieved about not getting the benefits. Therefore, I request the hon. Home Minister
to constitute a regulatory body to be approached whenever a person does not get justice

I quote, “In october 1947, accession took place. Soon atter that took place, the
Maharaia set up an emergency administration the head of which was Sheikh Mohammed
Abdulla, the leader of the most popular party in Kashmir. In March 1948, he substituted for
this emergency administration what he called a popular interim Government, consisting of
a Council of Ministers. He called Sheikh Mohammed Abdulla to accept the office of Prime
Minister and left it to him to choose his colleagues.” I again quote, "The point that I wish
to urge is that while two of these representatives would in any case under the present
rules be persons who could be nominated by the Ruler.." The Ruler was Maharaja. “We
are suggesting that all the four persons should be nominated by the Ruler on the advice
of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister happens to represent the largest political party
in the State. Apart from that, we have got to remember that the Prime Minister and his
Government are not based upon the Praja Sabha which is dead but based rather upon the
fact that they represent the largest political party in the State. Therefore, it is only appropriate
that the head of this party, who is also the Prime Minister, should have the privilege of
advising the Ruler as to who would be the proper representative of Kashmir in the
Constituent Assembly.”

Demand for providing medical assistance to State of Bihar and other States in
aftermath of outbreak of A.E.S.
SHRI ANIL DESAI (Maharashtra): Sir, it is very sad and outrageous that more than
130 young children died in Bihar’s Muzzafarpur due to deadly disease AES or  chamki.
This is not the first time but several deaths have occurred due to the same disease in
previous years also in this area. It seems health authorities remained negligent when

Special Mentions

470 [RAJYA SABHA]
reports of outbreak of AES spreading among children were pouring in from Samastipur ,
East Champaran, Vaishali and Muzzafarpur. The problem needs special ef forts not only
from the State Government but the Central Government must also shoulder the responsibility
to guide and provide expert medical advice to the S tate Government. A detailed full-
fledged investigation must be carried out in the country, particularly in Bihar, by experts to
ascertain the cause of recurring nature of this child disease, and find out whether lack of
cleanliness, malnourishment, litchi consumption or any other reason is responsible for
these unfortunate deaths. We are spending very, very less for our public health. Ordinary
people, whether educated or uneducated, urbanite or of rural background, must be aware
of basic norms to keep our surrounding hygienic and clean. Health must be our priority
number one than any other issue. According to NHP 2018, one doctor is serving 28,391
persons in Bihar whereas in Delhi, the figure stands at 1:11,000. The WHO norm of doctor-
patient ratio is one doctor for 1,000 patients. Remember that children are our future and if
they are not healthy, our nation cannot be healthy and it would also not prosper . Thank
you.
